newsitem.title: CANADA: Newbridge dips on lower Q1 estimates. [CORRECTED 01:45 GMT 7/8]
newsitem.headline: Newbridge dips on lower Q1 estimates. [CORRECTED 01:45 GMT 7/8]

text.p: Shares in Newbridge Networks Corp dropped in heavy trading following Tuesday's release of preliminary estimates which showed its first quarter figures would not meet analysts' expectations.

Newbridge fell 5.05, or more than seven percent, to 64.60 on more than 1.6 million shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange. On the New York Stock Exchange (corrects from Nasdaq) it lost 3.94 to 46.63 in thinner volume.
"The news is not that bad," said Eagle & Partners analyst Emil Savov. "This is a temporary glitch."

Newbridge Networks said that sales from its recently acquired UB Networks unit, in Santa Clara, California, would not meet company expectations. UB and related VIVID products help facilitate high-speed traffic on corporate networks.

The drop would not be offset by a 40 percent revenue increase in its public carrier network product, the MainStreetXpress 36170 Multiservices Switch, it said. Newbridge's first quarter ended August 3 and results are due to be released on August 19.
Yorkton Securities analyst Byron Berry said investors could assume that Newbridge's first-quarter earnings would drop five percent from the pre-charge profit of C$0.38 a share in the fourth quarter.
Analysts' estimates were higher than the C$0.36 (US$0.25) to C$0.37 (US$0.28) a share now forecast by the company, he added.
Berry said he remained optimistic about the company's ability to grow its UB networks unit.

Savov added that he believed the stock was correcting to a lower, more appropriate level after its run-up to a 52-week high of C$72.20 at the end of July in Toronto. Shares rose from a low of C$30.75.
"The stock is going down to where it should be, instead of being punished," said Savov, who has a 12-month target price of C$76.
